newsitem.title: USA: Talley rejects proposal for stock buyback.
newsitem.headline: Talley rejects proposal for stock buyback.

text.p: Talley Industries Inc on Tuesday rejected a proposal by a Saudi investor calling for the company to buy back seven million shares of its common stock.

In a statement, the company said the proposed self-tender offer would not be permitted under the terms of the company's existing loan covenants, and would be inconsistent with the company's plans for the next several years.
Earlier, Saudi investor Saad Alissa proposed that Talley use the $172 million it recently received from sales and litigation to buy back at least 7 million shares at $12.11 each in the first quarter.

Under the proposal, the company would buy back at least seven million shares at $12.11 each during the first three months of 1997, using a portion of the $154 million received in litigation with TRW Inc. and $18 million received from the sale of real estate.
